title: fix(ui): give painted ribbon cells and dropdowns AccessKit nodes
body:
Stacked on #2027 (merge #2027 first)

## What changed
- Attached AccessKit `Button` info (enabled, toggled/selected state, label) in `painted::cell`.
- Added `painted::menu_item` so custom-painted dropdown rows expose `Role::MenuItem` with enabled and toggled states.
- Annotated section drop rows, machine mode drop rows, ribbon tooltips (`set_description`), and workspace tabs (`Role::Tab` with `set_selected`) in `panes.rs`.
- Switched View `Panels`, Recent files, and Theme dropdown rows in `layout/mod.rs`, `recent_drop.rs`, and `theme_drop.rs` to `painted::menu_item`.
- Added 6 pinning tests in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/ribbon_accesskit.rs`.
- Replaced geometry-computing clicks in ribbon behaviour tests (`tests.rs`, `first_setup.rs`, `layout.rs`, `machines_pane.rs`, `recent_door.rs`, `setup_picks_disarm.rs`, `theme_door.rs`) with AccessKit role-and-label lookups.
- Left only the two pure layout/reach tests (`every_kind_has_a_home_on_every_machine` and `every_section_lives_behind_its_door_at_every_width`) on `ribbon_cells` and `mill_plan_at`.
- Scoped 7 existing UI tests (`tests.rs`, `fixtures_page.rs`, `machine_page.rs`, `setups_declutter.rs`, `structural.rs`, `theme_door.rs`, `unsaved.rs`) to their panel, modal prompt, or non-tab role so new ribbon button nodes do not collide with same-named buttons.
- Recorded the design choices in `docs/decisions/1988-ribbon-accesskit.md`.

## Cause
Custom-painted ribbon cells, workspace tabs, and ribbon dropdown rows used `ui.allocate_rect` or `ui.interact` without `WidgetInfo` or `AccessKitNodeBuilder` labels. title: feat(tools)!: cutting data by work material - Unknown default row, stepdown/stepover, stock material
body:
## What changed

Tool cutting data by work material (#2015, part of #2007):

- **`Unknown` row.** Every tool's cutting data now holds an `Unknown` row (file word `unknown`; in code `CuttingRow::material == None`). It is what the tool runs when no row names the material in force, and the fallback for a row's missing stepdown/stepover. It is derived from the tool's own rpm/feed and stored only when it states something more (other numbers, or a step) - so a new tool has it, every older tool reads its own numbers as it, and plain tools are stored, saved and shown to MCP byte for byte as before. A command that moves the running numbers away from a derived row stores it first. A waterjet (recipes) and an electrode (rpm 0) get none, so a sane tool never turns insane.
- **Stepdown and stepover per row** (mm, optional). They seed an operation's stepdown/stepover only inside an undoable command (quick-add, MCP `add_operation`, the feature recognizer, `SetWorkMaterial`, `SetStockMaterial`, retargeting a tool), never on load. Seeded kinds: pocket, adaptive, offset, slot, 3-D pocket, multi-axis rough, face (stepover; stepdown only when staged), 2-D contour (stepdown). A stepover wider than the cutter is refused by tool name.
- **Setup stock material.** New `StockMaterial` component on a setup's stock and the undoable `SetStockMaterial` command (MCP `set_stock_material`, stock page "Material" group). The row is picked by the stock's material, then the document's, then `Unknown`. The tools' running rpm/feed (the posted S word) follow the document material only - a tool is shared by every setup.
- **`.camtools`/project migration.** `PROJECT_VERSION` 62 -> 63 (the issue's "61 to 62" predates #1453's bump). A v62 project loads with each tool's own rpm/feed as its `Unknown` row; nothing it runs moves. `.camtools` reader accepts versions 1, 2 and 3; the writer writes 3 only when a library holds a stated `Unknown` row or a step (otherwise 1, or 2 for left-hand taps, as before). An `Unknown` row that only repeats the tool's own rpm/feed is not written, so plain tools save byte for byte as before (MCP `get_job` output unchanged for them).
- **Tool page.** The "Cutting data by material" group is now a table: Material, Spindle rpm, Feed, Stepdown, Stepover (0 = not stated). The `Unknown` row is first, its material fixed, not removable.
- **Behaviour change, inside a command only:** stating a document material the tool has no row for now runs the tool's `Unknown` row (before: the previous material's numbers stayed). An operation's milling feed still moves only for a row that names the material (#890's rule), so picking a material never overwrites hand-set op feeds.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2015-unknown-cutting-row.md` (why `Option<WorkMaterial>` and not a `WorkMaterial::Unknown` variant: `WorkMaterial::row()` indexes the handbook table).

Base: upstream/main (`31f8d03d7`); no file overlap with #2029 (it does not touch `tool_cutting_rows.rs`; both touch `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in different places). Fork synced at the current upstream main for this branch.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/tools/tests/unknown_row.rs` (6): selection order, step fallback, derivation once and only from the running numbers, kinds that get none, refusals (bad steps, `Unknown` twice).
- `crates/app/tests/cutting_unknown_row.rs` (9): `a_new_tool_gets_its_unknown_row_from_its_own_numbers`, `a_v62_project_loads_its_tool_numbers_as_the_unknown_row_with_no_loss`, `a_v1_tool_library_loads_with_the_unknown_row_and_steps_write_v3`, `the_row_is_picked_by_the_stock_then_the_document_then_unknown`, `a_second_setup_stock_material_seeds_only_its_own_operations`, `steps_seed_only_in_commands_and_the_stock_material_round_trips`, `a_project_with_no_new_rows_posts_the_same_s_and_f_words` (posts, re-saves as v62, reloads, re-posts: identical S/F words), `a_stated_stepover_wider_than_the_cutter_is_refused_by_tool_name`, `mcp_sets_the_stock_material_as_one_undo_step`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_material.rs`: the stock page's Material group sits between Shape and Size, and a pick is one undoable `SetStockMaterial`.
- Updated to the new law: `crates/app/tests/tool_cutting_rows.rs` (stating plastics, which has no row, now runs the tool's Unknown row), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutting_rows.rs` unit tests (Unknown is shown, never added).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (macOS, m5): green on 75031d5f9 (tools, app and ui suites; 6.2 min). Clippy on camcraft-tools, camcraft-app, camcraft-ui: clean (`--all-targets -D warnings`).

## Not exercised

- No hands-on UI run of the new table or the stock Material picker (unit/structural suites only); the pixel snapshots were not run (release lane) and no PNG changed.
- The camcraft-mcp skill row for `set_stock_material` is a follow-up (process-file change): #2076.
- A per-setup spindle speed (the S word by stock material) is out of scope: the tool's running rpm follows the document material.

Changelog: Tools keep cutting data per work material with an Unknown default row, an optional stepdown and stepover per row, and a setup stock may state its own material, which picks the row (stock, then document, then Unknown); older projects and tool libraries load unchanged (#2015)

Effort: high (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: project files are written as version 63 (and tool libraries with a stated Unknown row or steps as version 3); older builds refuse them.

Fixes #2015

title: fix(xtask): share one job budget across the lanes of a gate wave
body:
## What changed

- New `xtask/src/budget.rs`: one job budget for each gate run. The default is 6 (`budget::DEFAULT`). `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=<n>` (1 or more) overrides it. A bad value prints a note and keeps 6.
- `exec.rs` sets `-j` and `--test-threads=` of each step when it runs the step (`budget::scale`):
  - A wave of N lanes gives each lane `budget / N` jobs, minimum 1.
  - A step that runs alone gets the full budget. This applies to each quick, batch and test step, and to each release step that runs alone.
  - A value that a step sets on purpose (not the plan default `6`) can only go down.
- `lanes::waves(steps, limit)` takes the lane limit. The release tier gives `budget::lane_limit` = `budget / 2`, minimum 1. `LIMIT = 4` is removed. A budget of 6 gives 3 lanes of 2 jobs.
- The gate prints the budget line at the start, and `-- wave K: N lane(s) x -j M` before each wave. `--dry-run` prints the same lines.
- The `gate` and `runners` skills have the rule: the sum of `-j` of all builds on one machine stays at or below its core count.
- `docs/decisions/2057-gate-job-budget.md` records the choices.

## Overlap with #1952 (#1941)

The plan builders (`plan.rs`, `quick.rs`, `single.rs`) do not change. The executor rewrites the flags at run time. Thus each step that #1952 adds also gets the budget. `git merge-tree` of this branch with the head of #1952 is clean, so this PR does not stack on it. After the two PRs merge, one line of `docs/decisions/1941-gate-step-per-binary.md` ("four at most") is old. The cut can correct it when it collects the decisions.

## Readings

`cargo xtask gate release --dry-run` (start):

```
gate budget: 6 job(s) (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS overrides); at most 3 lane(s) per wave; 1 lane(s) x -j 6, 2 lane(s) x -j 3, 3 lane(s) x -j 2
-- wave 1: 1 lane(s) x -j 6
[01] debug build (--no-run)
...
-- wave 3: 3 lane(s) x -j 2
[03] geometry suites
     (cwd issue-2057) cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-geometry --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=2
```

`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4 cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run` prints `gate budget: 4 job(s); steps run one at a time with -j 4` and `-j 4 ... --test-threads=4` on each step.

title: fix(post): implement AC table-table inverse kinematics solver
body:
## What changed
Added the `camcraft_post::kinematics` module in `crates/post/src/kinematics/`.
Implemented `forward_machine` and `forward_part` using Rodrigues axis-angle rotation with configurable rotary axes, offsets, work datum, and rotary sign conventions.
Implemented `AcSolver` and `analytical_branches` to evaluate both `(+A, C)` and `(-A, C + 180 deg)` branches against `A.travel` and `C.travel`.
Added modal `C` holding inside `pole_sin_tol` near `A = 0` and weighted angular step minimization across branches for smooth zero crossings.
Added continuous `C` unwrapping inside sections, safe-retract re-wrapping, named refusals for invalid geometry or travel overflow, and quarter-point chord subdivision in `solve_path` and `solve_toolpath`.
Exported `kinematics` in `crates/post/src/lib.rs`, added tests in `crates/post/tests/ac_trunnion_ik.rs` and `crates/post/src/kinematics/tests.rs`, and recorded the design decision in `docs/decisions/1965-ac-trunnion-ik.md`.

## Cause
The codebase lacked a shared pure-Rust XYZAC table-table inverse kinematics solver in `camcraft-post`, so machine checking and post processors had no common kinematic core for off-pivot offsets, rotary branch selection, pole holding, continuous C unwrapping, and chord subdivision.

## Tests
- Pins (`cargo test -p camcraft-post --test ac_trunnion_ik`): 7 passed (`round_trip_fk_ik_with_nonzero_offsets_within_micron`, `asymmetric_a_limits_select_reachable_branch_and_refuse_unreachable`, `pole_near_zero_holds_previous_modal_c_instead_of_snapping_to_zero`, `smooth_crossing_of_a_zero_without_180_deg_c_flip`, `continuous_c_unwrapping_and_safe_retract_rewrapping`, `subdivides_linear_moves_beyond_chord_tolerance_for_tip_accuracy`, `refuses_malformed_machine_geometry_and_non_finite_inputs`).
- Unit tests (`cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib kinematics`): 4 passed (`rollover_wraps_into_0_to_360_at_initial_and_safe_retract`, `positive_only_a_limits_reorient_c_at_pole_within_chord_tolerance`, `solve_toolpath_converts_cl_moves_and_detects_retract`, `refuses_non_positive_path_options_and_parallel_spindle`).

- Mutation checks on `ac_trunnion_ik`:

## What changed

Fanuc, Doosan DNM and Mazak refuse a positive G83 dwell by name.

title: fix(2d): clear Zigzag rest boundaries without wall cusps
body:
Stacked on #1817 (merge #1817 first)

## What changed

2D rest machining now accepts Zigzag. It cuts rows, then closes each rest boundary to clear wall cusps.

Rows use an inset of `min(0.01 mm, stepover / 4)`. This prevents numeric boundary crossings without removing interior rows from small pockets.

The existing plain-pocket row algorithm moves unchanged to `pocket_zigzag.rs`. `pocket.rs` stays at 398 lines. No dependency is added.

The MCP skill now describes Zigzag support. Adaptive still has its named refusal. The entered previous tool remains an explicit trust assumption.

The remaining #1490 work has separate issues: Adaptive #2031, entry from cleared space #2032, and previous-operation stock #2033.

## Cause

Rows alone leave cusps at the rest boundary. A closing pass clears them. Rows that touch the boundary can cross it through numeric rounding.

A fixed 0.01 mm inset removes all rows from a tiny pocket. The stepover cap preserves those rows.

The geometry follows this project's existing scan and offset routines. See Held's [Zigzag Pocket Machining](https://www.cosy.sbg.ac.at/~held/projects/pocket_zig/pocket.html) and [pocket geometry monograph](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-54103-9). [Yao, Gupta and Nau](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~nau/papers/yao2003algorithms.pdf) provide the cutter-coverage context. The inset and closing-pass choices are ours.

## Tests

- `zigzag_rest_covers_corner_residue_without_gouges_or_unsafe_rapids`: red at the original refusal. Green after the fix. Covers both directions and 1.5/4 mm steps.
- `tiny_rest_pocket_keeps_interior_rows_when_previous_tool_fits_nowhere`: red with the fixed inset. Green with the stepover cap.
- Expected-change tests now accept Zigzag at the motion and operation parameter doors.
- Closing-pass mutation: red coverage; restored green. The first fixture left 287 measured residue points uncut.
- Zero-inset mutation: red verifier, with six crossings; restored green.
- Fixed-inset mutation: red tiny-pocket center coverage; restored green.
- Old `upstream/main` pocket code: red; restored green.
- Old `base-1817` rest strategy: red refusal; restored green. The parent baseline supplies the export absent from `upstream/main`.

The requested `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all three steps in 34.4 minutes before the inset cap.

After the cap, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only motion` passed its affected motion step in 663 seconds.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final code.

## Goldens moved

None from #1490. The diff against `base-1817` changes no `.nc` or `.cl` file.

The two-dot diff against `upstream/main` lists 147 files. All were checked against the merge base and parent.
Of these, 146 exactly reverse upstream changes absent from the older parent branch. The other is #1817's unchanged `pocket_rest_corners.cl` addition.

## Not exercised

No real machine was used. This change does not implement new Adaptive paths, cleared-space entry, or previous-operation stock input.
Those features require separate depth and cutter-clearance proofs in #2031, #2032, and #2033.

## Overlaps

- #1817 changes `rest_pocket`, `rest_strategy`, and the expected-refusal tests. This branch stacks on its head.
- #2013 and #1954 touch the same file, different module declarations in `machining2d/mod.rs`; whichever merges second refreshes.
- #1738 touches the same file, a different section of the MCP skill; whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1490-rest-strategies.md`.

Changelog: 2D rest Zigzag clears wall cusps with closing passes and preserves interior rows in small pockets.

title: feat(motion): cut the adaptive stock ring from the air (issue 1950, rounds A-B)
body:
﻿Draft. Rounds A to E of issue #1950 (a default whole-model Adaptive 3D Pocket exceeds the planner budgets on the stock ring). This PR does not close the issue: the D plate level still goes to the Offset rings, now by the hop budget. Round F is open.

Head: c3509172c331eedacbf61f8a07855cadd12fdb75

## What changed

Round A (motion crate):
- New planner `plan_from_air` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs`. It cuts the stock ring from the air side inward. Sources: Held 1991 (LNCS 500), Held and Spielberger 2009 (CAD 41(7)), Stori and Wright 2000.
- `Raster::open_air` marks the air band as open. The walk functions of `raster.rs` moved to `raster/walk.rs` with no change of logic.

Round B (plumbing, no new algorithm):
- `machining3d::open_sides` takes a `stock_band` argument. `machining3d::stock_band(r, adaptive)` gives `2r + OPEN_SLACK` for Adaptive and `r - OPEN_SLACK` for each other strategy.
- New entry `machining3d::pocket3d_open_prev(facets, footprint, stock, p, mask)`. The stock goes through `ladder`, `hsm::plan_level`, `adaptive_passes` and `hsm_passes`.
- A plan from the air whose worst reading is over the load bound is refused by name. The level then goes to the Offset rings with a note.

Round C:
- App arm (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, `open_side.rs`): a whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy (not shell, not rest roughing) uses the wide band and calls `pocket3d_open_prev` with the setup stock outline. Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and each other strategy keep the old band.
- Microlift joins (`adaptive/air_links.rs`): each pass is joined to the one before it by the existing `LinkLaw`. Each join is walked again on the stock. A pass with no proved join keeps its retract hop. Source: Otkur and Lazoglu 2007.

Round D:
- Air entry: `machining2d::in_air(stock, e, r)`. Where the first pass of an air plan starts 0.005 mm clear of the stock outline, the ladder enters the level by an axial plunge there. A tool that is not centre-cutting keeps the old entry law.
- Fixture refusal: `air_band_refusal` refuses the Adaptive whole-model op at generation when a tagged fixture meets the air band. The message starts with `AIR_BAND_FIXTURE` and names the fixture. The post gate is not changed.

Round E:
- Cause of the round D crossing at (-8.12, -35.61). A probe printed the crossing pairs of the air passes before and after the joins. Before the joins: 40 pairs. After the joins: the same 40 pairs. So the joins and the air entry did not cause it. Pass 0 is the spiral (3 closed fronts and a closing lap on ring 3 at y -35.607). Passes 1-21 are open-front runs. Passes 22-45 are wall laps. The pairs were:
  - the spiral and the first open runs: a lead-in starts one load width back, on the ring 3 lap, and steps past it;
  - each open run and the run of the next front (1-4, 4-7, ...);
  - open runs and wall laps (4-37, 7-22, ...): a run that meets the part wall cuts across the laps.
- Fix, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_uncross.rs` (new): each new pass drops the chords that cross a kept pass, by the plan's own law (`guard::crosses`). The pass then continues as a new piece. Each piece is read on the stock as before, so the rest and the load readings stay true. Result: 0 crossing pairs before the joins.
- The joins: with the bare passes clean, `LinkLaw::late` (a lead whose graze joins the pass) put crossings back, because the lead runs back across an earlier pass. `air_joins` now keeps a late join only when the grown pass crosses no other pass. If it crosses, the join falls back to the retract hop. Result: 0 crossing pairs after the joins.
- The crossing check, the load check, the verify gate and the budgets are not changed.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs` (427 lines) is split. The landing spots (wall margin, spots along the first pass, the helix placement, the plunge spot) move to `machining3d/descent_place.rs` (120 lines) with no change of logic. `descent.rs` is now 327 lines.

## Readings, round E (D plate, R = 5, 70 x 70 stock, one level, debug)

| Reading | Round C/D (crossing plan) | Round E |
|---|---|---|
| Crossing through `adaptive_passes` | at (-8.12, -35.61) | none |
| Passes | 47 | 61 |
| Retract hops (budget 8) | 3 | 23 |
| Worst load (of D) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) |
| Slack to the bound | 0.00135 deg | 0.00135 deg |
| Moves (budget 120000) | 17614 | 17549 |
| Cut / air / lift (mm) | - / - / 107.3 | 2632 / 338 / 108 |
| Rest (limit 0.02) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| Time, one level (debug) | 21.8 s | 22.0 s |
| Strategy of the level | Offset rings (crossing) | Offset rings (hop budget) |

22 of the 23 hops are late joins that were refused because their lead crosses an earlier pass. The earlier reading of 3 hops came from joins whose leads crossed. The hop budget was not raised.

## Posted G-code

- Changed. Each whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy and a stock outline uses the wide band. A level whose air plan is clean and in its budgets is cut from the air. Other levels go to the Offset rings by name, as before.
- On the D plate, the stock ring level is still cut by the Offset rings (by name, now for the hop budget).
- Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and the non-Adaptive strategies post as before.

## Pinning tests

title: fix(tools): preserve tap hand and refuse left-hand posting
body:
Stacked on #2001 (merge #2001 first)

## What changed

Store explicit tap hand on the tool.
Default older tools to right-hand.
Refuse malformed hand values by name.
Preserve hand through catalog import, tool JSON, project files, tool libraries, editor drafts and undoable commands.
Show the left-hand choice in the tap editor.
State that left-hand posting is unavailable.

Refuse left-hand taps in the shared posting preflight before records or NC files are emitted.
The refusal names the operation and tool.
It covers all eight built-in posts that implement tapping: Fanuc, Haas, Siemens 840D, Heidenhain, Mazak, Tormach PathPilot, Doosan DNM and Fanuc Lathe.
Right-hand output stays unchanged.

Write project version 62 for saved projects.
Use library version 2 only for exports containing a left-hand tap.
These versions make older readers refuse the files instead of silently losing hand.
Keep right-hand-only libraries at version 1.

## Cause

The tool model had no tap hand.
The tool JSON reader silently discarded an unknown hand field.
A left-hand declaration therefore could not survive the existing data path.
Every supported tapping cycle used the right-hand assumption.

title: fix(fidelity): a stock copy of an incomplete model keeps naming its hole
body:
A stock copied from an incomplete model (#1610) now keeps naming that model's hole after the model is deleted. Before this change, its refusal at the post fell back to "saved before CamCraft recorded mesh fidelity (project v58 or older)". The post still refused it; only the reason given was wrong.

Fixes #1700

## What changed

The copy's refusal read the hole from the source model by name (`mesh_open::unknown_note`), so once the source was gone the lookup found nothing. Now the copy carries the hole itself (`schema::MeshOpen`), beside the fidelity-unknown sentinel it already carried (#1056):

- **Where the hole is copied:** every place that lands the sentinel on a copy now lands the hole with it:
  - `SetStock` and its undo
  - a setup clone (`CreateSetup` with a datum)
  - an undone `DeleteSetup`
  - `UpdateModel`'s refresh of the copies, and its undo
  - the project loader
- **Where the refusal reads it:** `model_fidelity::op_problem` reads the hole off the entity that carries the sentinel. Two small helpers: `mesh_open::hole_behind` (the twin of `model_fidelity::chord_behind`) and `mesh_open::note_for`.
- **Project file:** the saver already wrote `mesh_open` for any entity that has one. The loader now also accepts it on a `FromModel` stock marked `fidelity_unknown`, and a hole without the mark stays corrupt. There is no version bump: #1610's check (a hole on anything but a model is corrupt) has not shipped in a cut yet, so no released reader refuses these files.

The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/1700-stock-copy-hole.md`.

## How tested

- **New:** `crates/app/tests/stock_copy_hole.rs` (6 tests). A copy carries the hole, and its refusal names the source and the hole:
  - after the source is deleted, and across undo and redo of that delete;
  - after save, load, and a second save that matches byte for byte;
  - through a setup clone and an undone setup delete;
  - through a whole re-import of the source (which clears it) and that re-import's undo;
  - through `SetStock`'s undo.

  The file also checks that a stock with a hole and no mark fails to load as corrupt.
- **Without the fix,** the two "source deleted" tests fail: the refusal reads "saved before CamCraft recorded …".
- **Existing tests:** the `import_step_open_shell` tests from #1610 still pass. Its corrupt-file message check passes too, because the new message keeps the old wording as a prefix.
- **Gate:** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (112 app suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branched from upstream/main after #1699 merged, not from a cut tag: the code this fixes is not in v0.20.0.

title: fix(ui): lay a lathe's spindle axis across the viewport
body:
## What changed

The cause of #1993 is in the camera, not in the envelope. The envelope already is a cylinder about world Z for a lathe (`crates/post/src/machine/envelope.rs:27-60`). The turning paths also use world Z as the spindle axis. But `Camera::basis_right` (`crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`, before this PR: `normalize([fy, -fx, 0.0])`) always crossed the view with world +Z. Thus world Z could never lie across the screen, and each cylinder about Z stood vertical.

- New `crates/ui/src/view_frame.rs`: `ViewFrame { Mill, Lathe }`, a proper rotation between the orbit frame and the world. `Mill` is the identity. `Lathe`: local x = world -Z, local y = world +Y, local z = world +X.
- `Camera` gets a `frame` field. `eye` and `basis_right` map through the frame. `basis_up`, `mvp`, `ray_through`, `dolly_cursor`, the traced-stock eye and the view cube read that one basis. Draw and pick stay on one matrix.
- `Camera::toward` converts the world direction of the view cube into the frame. `Camera::pan` now uses the Z part of the right vector (it was always zero before).
- `Camera::with_frame` sets a frame and its home view. `view_frame::sync` runs at the top of `viewport_panel` in each frame. It reads `camcraft_app::machine::kind_of` (the machine of the active setup). A change of frame takes the home view of the frame. Fit and "nothing to frame" keep the frame.
- Screen rule for a lathe: the right-handed program frame (ISO 841) does not change. The home view puts world +Z (the spindle axis, away from the chuck) to the right and world +X (the cross-slide) up. World +Y then points to the viewer. The frame comes from the machine kind in the machine data, not from a hard-coded hand per machine.

Display only. The world, the WCS, the toolpaths and the posted G-code do not change: no post or generator code reads `Camera`. The frame change is view state, not a command (the test checks that the history does not change).

The decision record is `docs/decisions/1993-lathe-envelope-axis.md`.

## What #2019 still needs

This PR does the camera part. #2019 stays open for:

- The world gizmo: show Z and X only on a lathe, and Y only when the machine has a Y axis.
- A decision for mill-turn machines (this PR keeps them in the milling frame).
- View cube face names for the lathe frame, if the maintainer wants them (the cube now names world directions in each frame).
- The pin that the posted program of a turning golden does not change.

## Overlap

PR #2006 changes `crates/ui/src/work_envelope.rs`. This PR does not touch that file. PR #1689 changes `Camera::eye` and `Camera::mvp` in `crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`. This PR changes `Camera::eye` too, so a small merge conflict can occur in `eye`.

## Refresh (merge of main 17a8c6e76)

- New head: 4eb577be305761c352696384cf4426ae8f207de4 (old head c620c1255b710ce1bce0e368c542c94db255f901).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`: both sides added a test module after `mod work_envelope;`. The merge keeps the two: `mod lathe_view;` (#1993) and `mod camera_target;` (#1997).
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs` merged without a conflict. `reset_for_open` now calls `frame_all` (#1997). `frame_all` keeps the camera frame (this PR), and `view_frame::sync` keeps the target and the distance. Thus an open frames the part, and a lathe keeps its frame.
- Tests after the merge (debug, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, filters lathe_view, camera_target, view_frame, work_envelope, camera, frame, viewcube, orbit, pan): 63 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. This includes `lathe_view::*` (3 tests), `camera_target::frame_target_is_the_same_with_the_envelope_on_and_off` and `camera_target::open_frames_the_part_with_the_envelope_on_and_off`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Delta class: DELTA (one hand-resolved file, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`).

## Tests

Pinned by these tests in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/lathe_view.rs`:

- `a_lathe_lays_the_envelope_along_the_spindle_axis_left_to_right`: through the real shell, a lathe machine file gives the lathe frame and its home view. Screen right is world +Z and screen up is world +X. The envelope ends stay at the Z travel (-197, 3). The projected spindle axis is level, +Z is to the right, and the X radius goes up. The history does not change.
- `a_mill_again_takes_the_milling_view_back`: a mill machine file again gives the milling frame and the house isometric.
- `the_lathe_frame_keeps_pick_pan_and_the_view_cube_on_one_basis`: in the lathe frame, the basis is orthonormal and right-handed, the centre ray hits the target, a pan moves along the spindle axis, and the view cube and orbit keep the frame.

Existing tests run (debug, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, filters law_tests, viewcube, eye_geom, view_names, orbit, pan, iso, box_select, one_pick_rule, wcs_circle, wcs_part_point, wcs_pick_click, work_envelope, frame, edge_click, review_1710, camera, lathe_view): 144 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No visible app window was opened. The screenshots below come from an offscreen render.
- The pixel snapshots (release lane) are not run. The lathe view does not change a mill snapshot.

Changelog: The viewport shows a lathe with its spindle axis from left to right and the cross-slide up, so the work envelope lies along the spindle axis (#1993).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1993

## Screenshots

Method: the real shell and the viewport, rendered offscreen at 1280x800 by the UI test harness. No app window was opened. The same steps run before and after: mount a lathe machine with Z travel -197 to 3, turn on "Show work envelope", then set the camera target to (0, 0, -97) and the distance to 420.

Before (origin/main, 2f6de7c5b). The envelope cylinder stands upright:

![before: lathe envelope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/1f3a51015cc13780c217388ed587a932e61ee5ea/pr-2023/lathe-before.png)

After (this PR, c620c1255). The spindle axis runs left to right. The cylinder lies along it:

![after: lathe envelope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/1f3a51015cc13780c217388ed587a932e61ee5ea/pr-2023/lathe-after.png)

title: fix(ui): prevent tool editor width growth from numeric overflow
body:
Stacked on #2001 (merge #2001 first)

## What changed

Keep oversized numeric controls aligned to the start of their allocated space.
The tool editor keeps its width across 100 frames with the pointer moving.
The fix changes `fields::num_sized` and preserves its width budgets and unit conversion.
The issue commit changes no tool editor column widths.
Record the decision in `docs/decisions/2003-tool-editor-width.md`.
Effort: low.

## Cause

The feed-rate `DragValue` exceeds the shared 96-point field budget when it draws `1800.0 mm/min`.
The old `ui.add_sized` centers the oversized control.
Its leading edge overflows by 1.8125 points.
That overflow feeds the next window layout and adds 1.8125 points per frame.
The existing tool editor grew from 770 to 951.25 points over 100 pointer frames.

## Tests

All four pins pass in the default UI value-test suite.

- `existing_tool_editor_width_stays_put_after_100_pointer_frames` failed before the fix.
- `new_tool_editor_width_stays_put_after_100_pointer_frames` covers the new-tool path and passes on both versions.
- `wide_metric_feed_tool_editor_width_stays_put_after_100_pointer_frames` covers a long metric feed.
- `wide_inch_feed_tool_editor_width_stays_put_after_100_pointer_frames` covers a long inch feed.

The mutation check copied the actual `upstream/main` version of `fields.rs` back into the worktree.
The existing-tool and both long-feed pins failed at runtime.
The wide metric case grew from 770 to 1314.8125 points.
The wide inch case grew from 770 to 1305.1563 points.
All four pins passed after restoring the fix.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all four steps with zero failures.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
The required gate also covers the inherited #2001 changes.

## Tool editor before and after pointer movement

These are 1280 × 720 headless renders of the shipping egui shell, captured with the existing-tool width-test setup and its 100 pointer-movement frames. The viewport is the harness placeholder. They are review evidence, separate from snapshot goldens.

The before renders use the original `num_sized` implementation from this issue commit's parent. The editor grows from 770 to 951.25 points. The after renders use this PR's fixed implementation. Its width stays at 770 points.

| Implementation | Initial frame | After 100 pointer frames |
|---|---|---|
| Before | ![Before: initial editor width 770 points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55/2020/before-initial.png) | ![Before: editor width grows to 951.25 points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55/2020/before-pointer100.png) |
| After | ![After: initial editor width 770 points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55/2020/after-initial.png) | ![After: editor width stays at 770 points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55/2020/after-pointer100.png) |

The four PNGs are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch at `92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55`. Temporary capture code was removed. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Goldens moved

None.
The NC and CL golden diff against `upstream/main` is empty.

## Not exercised

No manual native-window session or release-lane pixel snapshot was run.
The other floating dialogs received a source audit.
The machine editor, G-code viewer, post refusal, and Debug info windows specify default sizes or widths.
The fixture library and unsaved prompt cap their content widths.
The G-code viewer also bounds its trace columns.
The audit found no reason to change those dialogs in this issue.

## Overlaps

#2001 changes `tool_editor_window`, which was the expected edit site during the overlap check.
This branch starts at its head `028a0ad0e`.
The final fix lives in `fields::num_sized` instead.
#2001 must merge first.

#1931 touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
#1717 touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
Both change WCS properties in `pages.rs`.
The `pages.rs` changes in this branch come unchanged from #2001.
The overlap check found no open PR touching `fields.rs` or `tests/tool_cutter.rs`.

title: fix(ui): stand the work envelope on the table plane
body:
## What changed

The displayed mill envelope starts on the Z=0 table plane.
It keeps its full Z travel height.
X/Y keep the setup work origin as their reference.
Lathe cylinders keep their existing reference.
The tooltip states these references.
The decision record is in `docs/decisions/1963-envelope-table.md`.

## Cause

The viewport drew the program-space travel bounds directly.
Those bounds can extend below the table plane.
With `assets/machines/tormach-pcnc1100-s3.mch`, the fresh document implicit setup drew its bottom at Z=-419.1 mm.
X/Y have no equivalent height error against the table plane.
The current machine files do not state a table footprint for another X/Y reference.

No travel or reach check uses the drawn box.
`crates/post/src/machine/envelope.rs` supplies display data only.
The travel check in `crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs` reads axis limits and program coordinates directly.
This fix changes no safety check.

## Viewport screenshots

Both images use the Tormach PCNC 1100 Series 3 machine file.
Both use a fresh document, the implicit setup, and the world origin.
The work envelope is visible in both images.
The GPU viewport and the application UI render at 1440 × 960 pixels.
The camera stays fixed: target [0, 0, 180] mm, yaw 0.9 rad, pitch 0.5 rad, distance 2400 mm.
A temporary test fixture captured the application UI and GPU viewport.
The fixture was removed after capture.

Before: the display shift is reverted. The box bottom is Z=-419.1 mm.

![Before: envelope below the table plane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2006/before.png)

![After: envelope starts at the table plane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2006/after.png)

The images are stored only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.
The PR branch contains no screenshot files.

## Tests

`mill_envelope_stands_on_table_for_all_travel_files` failed before the fix.
It checks each bundled box envelope with complete travel limits.
It pins the bottom at Z=0, the travel height, and the existing X/Y bounds.

It ran 817 unit tests and 25 integration tests.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

title: fix(ui): frame the opened document so the orbit pivot is on the part
body:
## Cause

The work envelope (#1567, commit `c0b4dfc85`) does not move the camera target. No line puts it there:

- The envelope is overlay lines only: `crates/ui/src/work_envelope.rs` `envelope_lines`, added to `interact::collect_overlay` (`crates/ui/src/interact.rs:947`).
- `State::frame_all` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:3847`) reads only the facets of named entities and the WCS origins. It does not read the overlay or the machine.
- `Camera::orbit` turns about `Camera::target`. Only `frame_all`, pan, the wheel dolly and `actions::frame_at` write the target.

The pivot that the maintainer saw is the target that a document open left in place. `State::reset_for_open` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:4225`) did not touch the camera. After an open, the target stayed at the old document's target, or at the default target at the world origin. No commit changed this; it is the same in v0.20.0. With a machine mounted, the envelope box is drawn about the work origin, near that target. Thus the orbit looked as if it turned about the envelope and not about the part.

The new test reproduced this before the fix: after an open, the target stayed at the parked `[400, 400, 400]`, with the envelope display on and off.

## Fix

`reset_for_open` now calls `frame_all`, as the F key does. This applies to the disk open and the browser-bytes open (#1613). The status line still says `opened ...`. The envelope stays out of each camera bound.

## Answers to the brief

- The envelope display is off by default (`show_work_envelope: false`). With the box off, the envelope draws nothing and has no effect on the target. With the box on, it also has no effect on the target. The defect showed with the box on and off.
- Other bodies, checked against `frame_all`:
  - Fixtures and vises: they are facet entities, so they enter the frame. They did before #1567 too. They are physical bodies that the collision check reads, not display-only bodies. No change.
  - Machine table: the viewport draws no machine table body. Nothing to check.
  - Simulation tool body, toolpaths, height planes, the envelope: overlay or GPU parts only, not in the frame bounds.
- The orbit about the point under the pointer is not in this PR. It is filed as #1998 (enhancement, P6, effort:medium).
- #1963 and #1993 (envelope position and shape) are not touched.

## Pinning tests

In the default ui lib suite, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/camera_target.rs` (value tests, no pixel snapshot):

- `frame_target_is_the_same_with_the_envelope_on_and_off`: a mill with an asymmetric travel box is mounted. The frame target and distance are equal with the envelope on and off, and the target lies on the part and stock.
- `open_frames_the_part_with_the_envelope_on_and_off`: a saved document is opened with the camera parked far away. The target after open is equal with the envelope on and off, lies on the part and stock, and is equal to the F-key frame. Failed before the fix.

## Readings

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`): green, 1.0 min. ui lib 818 passed (6 ignored), and the suites boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, sinker_setup, theme_files all passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No GUI hand test. The orbit drag on a real window was not tried.
- No pixel snapshot lane (release only). No PNG changed.
- The camera after File > New and after an import is unchanged by this PR.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1997-envelope-camera-target.md`.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: A document open now frames the camera on the opened part and stock, so the orbit turns about the part and not about the old view's target.

Fixes #1997

## Screenshots

Method: an offscreen render of the real viewport (the test GPU path). No app window was opened. The project has a small part and a Tormach 770M, with the work envelope shown. Steps are the same before and after: open the project, then turn the camera by a fixed yaw of 0.9 rad.

After (this PR, e2d0797e9). The camera frames the part and stock. The target is (0, 0, 10) and the distance is 277.

title: fix(2d): Side Auto reads the material at the picked ring's own level
body:
The base is `main`. #1935 is merged (`cfc8447ee`), and this branch has `origin/main` merged in (`6bbed2171`).

## What changed

- Side Auto of a 2D Contour on picked rings now reads the part section at the rings' own level. It does not read the full XY silhouette. The floor of a blind bore filled that silhouette, so Auto resolved Outside on the bore rim and the #1927 law refused the pass.
- New law `machining2d::auto_side` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_auto.rs`):
  - It reads the section 0.01 mm under the top of the picks' Z span, then 0.01 mm over its bottom.
  - At each probe it compares the area inside the rings with a 0.5 mm band outside the rings. A side holds material at a fill of 0.5 or more.
  - Material inside only gives Outside. Material outside only gives Inside. The first probe that decides is the result.
  - If the two probes decide differently, or if they see material on both sides and do not decide, the generate is refused by name: "Side Auto cannot tell which side of the picked ring holds the material at Z ...: ... - set Side to Inside or Outside".
  - If no probe sees material on either side (a sheet part, a ring over the part in air), the part's XY outline decides, as before.
- New `crates/app/src/operation/contour_auto_pick.rs`: it reads the Z span of the picks (in the setup frame, or along a tilted frame's axis) and the material, and calls the law.
- `selection.rs` uses the new verdict in place of the old fill block. `generate.rs` refuses an Undecided verdict by name. `contour_auto_side` (the UI preview) maps Undecided to "no answer".
- The rule applies only to `OpParams::Contour` with Side Auto. Plasma and wire contours do not use this verdict.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1933-contour-auto-side-level.md`.

## Readings (tool centre to the wall, Ø6 tool, Side Auto, model top to model bottom)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Blind bore rim, Ø20 bore to floor Z 4, rim at Z 10 | Outside, refused "set Side to Inside" | Inside, centre 3.000 mm inside the wall (max error 0.000001), deepest level Z 4.000 (the floor), 0 gouges |
| Same bore, floor rim at Z 4 | Outside | Inside, same pass, deepest level Z 4.000, 0 gouges |
| Through hole Ø20 | Inside | Inside, centre 3.000 mm inside the wall, cut to Z 0, 0 gouges |
| Boss 20 x 20 on a floor at Z 5 | Outside | Outside, centre 3.000 mm outside the wall, cut to Z 5, 0 gouges |
| Block 40 x 40 outer wall | Outside | Outside, centre 3.000 mm outside the wall, cut to Z 0, 0 gouges |
| `Milling-test.step` bore rim r 12.5 at Z 20 (Ø10 tool) | Outside, refused | Inside, the same moves as Side Inside, centre 5.000 mm inside the rim, 0 warnings |

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/contour_auto_level.rs` (new, 3 tests): `auto_on_a_blind_bore_rim_cuts_the_wall_from_inside_to_the_floor`, `auto_on_a_through_hole_rim_cuts_inside`, `auto_on_a_boss_and_on_an_outer_wall_cuts_outside`.
- `crates/motion/tests/contour_auto_side.rs` (new, 6 tests): the law on boxes, the floor rim, the mid-solid refusal, the disagreeing probes refusal, the outline fallback and the empty part.
- `crates/app/tests/area_open.rs`: `a_containment_that_puts_the_tool_in_the_part_is_refused_by_name`. Its last assert now expects the clean Inside pass in place of the refusal.
- The #1935 refusals are unchanged: `contour_outside_hole` 5 of 5 pass.
- `operations.rs` 120 pass, 6 ignored. This includes the sheet-part tests `contour_boss_pick_defaults_outside`, `a_closed_chain_routes_the_boundary_path_not_a_centerline` and `selection_notes_report_stitching_and_extension`.

## Gate

Gate on head `6bbed21715b726e96ac39430b945e15e72bdc89f` (this branch with `origin/main` merged in, no hand edits in the merge). The touched test binaries ran one by one (debug, `-j 6`, `--test-threads=6`):

| Crate | Binary | Result |
|---|---|---|
| camcraft-app | `setup_align` | 10 pass |
| camcraft-app | `stitch_cross` | 6 pass |
| camcraft-app | `contour_auto_level` | 3 pass |
| camcraft-app | `area_open` | 11 pass |
| camcraft-app | `contour_outside_hole` | 5 pass |
| camcraft-app | `operations` | 120 pass, 6 ignored |
| camcraft-motion | `contour_auto_side` | 6 pass |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings` is clean.

The 2 app tests that were red on the old head `13a1f2625` now pass:
- `setup_align::unverified_kinds_are_refused_while_verified_picks_generate_aligned`
- `stitch_cross::a_self_touching_single_body_still_stops_at_its_top_level`

Cause: the old head was based on an earlier #1935 head. The last #1935 commit `72c8f293d` (now on main) changed these 2 tests for the #1927 refusal law, and changed `contour_depth.rs` to name an unreadable mesh. The merge of `origin/main` brought in that commit. This PR changes no assert of these 2 tests.

Earlier full quick gate on `13a1f2625` (36.6 min): post ok, motion ok, ui ok, app failed only in the 2 tests above.

title: fix(2d): refuse a picked contour ring whose side stands in the part
body:
﻿## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_depth.rs`: new `picked_law`. A picked ring that walks no level below the local part top is refused by name when the operation levels go below that top. The local top is the highest vertex of the facets near the ring (XY box plus the tool radius and the stock to leave).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs`: new entry point `contour_on_picked`. It runs the law after the depth ladder. `contour_on_part` and `contour_on_bodies` do not change.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: the Selection source of 2D Contour calls `contour_on_picked`. The whole-model source (entity or stock) does not change.
- `docs/decisions/1927-contour-picked-ring-law.md`: the decision and the dropped alternatives.

The refusal text names the ring position, the part top and the fix, for example: "the picked ring at (0.294, -12.986) meets its wall at no level below the part top Z 10.000: the cutter Outside this ring stands in the part material - if the ring bounds a hole, set Side to Inside; else check the tool containment". The side that the law reads is the resolved side (the app resolves Auto first), and a tool containment also moves the ring. Thus the text names the two causes.

Two existing tests pinned the silent top-plane pass and change:
- `crates/app/tests/area_open.rs`: on the rim of a blind bore, Side Auto resolves to Outside, and a forced Containment Outside puts the ring 10 mm into the wall. The two cases cut only the mouth, in air, with 0 warnings. They are now refused by name. Side Inside is the clean control. The test is renamed to `a_containment_that_puts_the_tool_in_the_part_is_refused_by_name`. The wrong Auto verdict on blind bores is #1933 (P3). This PR does not fix it.
- `crates/app/tests/tilt.rs`: the flat control used Inside on the top face of a block (the mirror case). It now uses Outside.

## Readings (main `d1484f02a`)

- Plate 60 x 60 x [0, 10], through hole D20, D6 end mill, stepdown 2.5.
- Side Outside on the hole wall walked only Z 10 and posted with status Ok, 0 warnings and 0 gouges. Full depth (Bottom of model) gave the same result.
- Cause: the depth ladder reads the material strictly above each level. At the part top no material is above, so each ring is legal there.
- The tip stayed on the top face, so the posted path did not gouge. It machined nothing that the user picked and said nothing.
- `verify` on the same ring forced down the full ladder reports Gouge warnings. The verifier has no gap, so no verifier issue is filed.
- Details are in the issue comment.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/contour_outside_hole.rs` (5 tests):

- `outside_on_a_picked_hole_wall_is_refused_by_name_at_every_depth` (chain pick and patch pick, full depth and selection heights)
- `inside_and_auto_on_the_hole_wall_cut_every_level_clean`
- `outside_on_an_outer_wall_and_on_a_boss_stays_legal`
- `inside_on_a_picked_block_top_is_refused_by_name`
- `the_full_depth_outside_ring_is_a_gouge_to_the_verifier`

Also pinned: `area_open::a_containment_that_puts_the_tool_in_the_part_is_refused_by_name`, `tilt::tilt_on_a_picked_selection_refuses_by_name`.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick`) on `dfceb20ac`: post suites ok (67 s), motion suites ok (777 s), app suites ok (775 s), 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `cargo fmt --check` is clean. The branch has a merge of `origin/main` (it takes the #1924 test repair). The last commit is docs only.

## Review fix (head 72c8f293d)

A quick gate on a tree with 0761173e8 had two red camcraft-app tests. On origin/main they cannot fail this way: the refusal text is not in main (`git grep` finds 0 hits).

- `setup_align::unverified_kinds_are_refused_while_verified_picks_generate_aligned`: the refusal is correct. The test picked the first horizontal face, the modelled top annulus (Z 20, hole 20 x 20). The setup flips the part over Y, so the annulus lies at the setup's Z 0 and the blind hole opens down (Z 0..10). Z 10..20 is solid 40 x 40. Outside of the hole ring, the cutter centre runs at +-8 mm, in that solid at Z 16 and Z 12. The old path kept only the top plane, in air. The law reads the setup frame: the same ring generates as modelled. The test now picks the modelled bottom face (the setup's top) with Side Outside and asserts a cut below Z 19.9. The annulus stays as a control: it generates as modelled and is refused by name after the flip. The Offset2D refusal and the Contour1 assert do not change.
- `stitch_cross::a_self_touching_single_body_still_stops_at_its_top_level`: the refusal gave the wrong cause. The ring is Outside of a 40 x 40 outline, and Outside is air. The ladder stopped the ring at Z 10 because the one self-touching shell cannot be sectioned at Z 0 (non-manifold slice error, fail closed). The law said "set Side to Inside", which is wrong advice. Fix: `contour_depth::ladder` keeps the slice error that stopped each ring (`Ladder::unread`). `picked_law` still refuses, but it names that error and the skipped levels, and does not name the side. The test asserts the refusal, `levels below skipped (0.000)`, `non-manifold`, and no Side advice. The one-block reference still cuts below the top.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`) on 72c8f293d: motion suites ok (843 s), app suites ok (785 s), setup_align and stitch_cross ok, 0 failed. - The MCP path and the GUI (the same generator runs under them).
- Multi-body picks with bodies of different heights.
- Auto on a blind bore is pinned as a refusal only (#1933 owns the verdict).
- The release lanes.

`contour.rs` was 446 lines before this PR (over the 400-line law). This PR adds 15 lines. A split is owed separately.

Changelog: 2D Contour refuses a picked ring whose side lies in the part at each level (Outside on a hole wall, Inside on a block outline), with the fix in the message. Before, it cut only the top plane and posted with no warning.

## What changed

Box stock with retained cut history now preserves machined walls and cavities through side-on quarter turns.
The carry retains swept-tool geometry and reads separate material intervals along the new columns.

The old carry knew column heights but lost the wall position between column centres.

- **Motion** (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_widen.rs`): `WireWidening { PerRuling, Uniform }`. `PerRuling` is the default. Each ruling stands off by what its own twist needs. Transition rulings 1 mm from the ends of a long span end the widening near the twist. The existing ruled kerf law judges the emitted wire at every height. A path that fails it is refused by name.
- **Sim** (`crates/sim/src/verify/wire/`): `WireJob.verify_tol`. The kerf law lets a reading enter the facets by no more than the stated tolerance. The threading law and the slug law do not use it. A tolerance that is negative, not finite or not below the kerf offset is refused as unreadable. A gouge names the deepest reading at any height.
- **App**: the 4-axis block stores `widening` and `verify_tolerance` (0 to 0.25 mm at the operation door). The two values go through `EditOperationParams` and the project file. The widening is in the stamp digest. The post gate's report line states the tolerance and the deepest reading that it let pass. A 4-axis gouge with no stated tolerance adds a hint that names the model's chord tolerance.
- **UI**: the operation page shows "Stand off" and "Verify tolerance" in the 4-axis block.
- **Docs**: `site/content/guide/operations-edm.md`, `docs/decisions/1170-wire-ruling-kerf.md`.

There is no new command. The MCP surface takes the two keys through the operation parameters DTO (`four_axis.widening`, `four_axis.verify_tolerance`).

## Readings

Motion, square 10 to round 8, 64 points, twist tolerance 0.05 mm:

- Per ruling: the middle of each side stands as a plain taper of its lean (less than 0.003 mm more than the kerf offset). The rulings next to the corners stand 0.015 to 0.05 mm more.
- Uniform: every ruling stands 0.0207 mm more. The note says `the wire is held 0.1857 mm off both profiles`.
- A punch with one twisted flank: `9 of 13 rulings stand within 0.0001 mm of the kerf offset`.

App, square 8 lofted toward a circle, faceted at a chord tolerance of 0.0117 mm:

- No tolerance: `Punch1: wire gouge: the kerf of move 2 enters the part by 0.0004 mm near X-8.019 Y-0.833 at Z2.001 (64 move(s) gouge; the deepest reading at any height is 0.0112 mm) - a tessellated loft's facets stand past its ruled surface by up to the chord tolerance of the model: ...`
- Tolerance 0.0028: refused, `..., past the stated verify tolerance 0.0028 mm (40 move(s) gouge; the deepest reading at any height is 0.0112 mm)`.
- Tolerance 0.0117: posts. The report line says `kerf judged under the stated verify tolerance 0.0117 mm: the kerf enters the model's facets by at most 0.0112 mm, near X-7.468 Y-7.980 at Z6.000`.
- Tolerance 0.2: refused, `the verify tolerance 0.2 mm is not zero or a positive number below the kerf offset 0.1650 mm`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `wire_edm::ruled_widen_tests`: `a_square_to_round_punch_is_widened_only_where_it_twists`, `only_the_twisted_flank_of_a_punch_is_widened`, `a_twisted_flank_ends_its_widening_at_the_transition_rulings`.
- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::wire::tol_tests` (5 tests).
- `camcraft-app` `wire_verify_tol`: `a_tessellated_loft_posts_under_its_chord_tolerance_and_is_refused_below_it`, `the_widening_and_the_tolerance_are_stored_and_bounded_at_the_door`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `wire_four_axis_states_the_stand_off_choice_and_the_verify_tolerance`.

Quick gate on the final head `fc6848cf0`, all green. Rerun on the final head: `camcraft-motion` lib `wire_edm` (33 passed), `camcraft-motion` test `wire_fans` (7 passed), `camcraft-ui` lib `wire` (15 passed, includes the pinning test). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. Results after the merge of main, from the worker: `camcraft-app` binaries `wire_verify_tol` (2), `wire_4axis` (8), `solid_law_goldens` (7) passed. Earlier results on the same app code: `camcraft-sim` lib `verify::wire` (20), `wire_fans` (2), `wire_stamp` (7), `golden_cl` (33), `project_roundtrip` (73), `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_contour`, `wire_post`, `wire_tabs`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_readers`, `edm_conditions`, `conformance`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `sodick_wire_post`. The clippy run of `camcraft-sim` and `camcraft-app` was clean earlier and was not run again.

## Screenshots

The operation page, Geometry tab, with the 4-axis block on. The images come from the test harness render. They are on the `screenshots` branch and are not part of this PR.

`crates/app/tests/golden/wire_4axis_punch.cl` and `golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_4axis_punch.nc` are regenerated. The pose words moved by microns (for example `-8167` to `-8166`). title: feat(ui): drag a part along an axis with move handles (#1198 b)
body:
#1198 slice (b): move handles with drag-to-move. Slice (a), the bottom bar, merged in #1203. Slice (c), the rotate handles, is #2047. Slice (d), snapping and typed values, stays on #1198.

**GUI hand check needed.** The kittest harness and headless state tests test the handles, the drag and the readout. The offscreen screenshots below come from the same harness. Nobody has examined them on a real screen with real mouse input.

## What changed
- **Move mode in the bottom bar.** A new bar button (a four-armed cross, after Pick through) turns `State::move_handles` on and off. It is off by default. It is view state like Pick through, and it queues no command.
- **Handles** (`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`, painted by `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`). With Move on and exactly one shown part selected, three arms in the axis colours start at the bounding-box centre of the part. Each arm ends in a ball. The arms stay 70 px long on screen at all zoom levels. The ball under the pointer is drawn larger.
- **Drag.** A press on a ball takes the press before orbit and pick. A press on empty space still orbits. When a nav tool of the bar (Orbit, Pan, Zoom) is latched, that tool owns the press. While the button is down, the preview moves the body along the axis (`world.rs` draws it with an offset) and never writes the world. The signed distance shows above the bar. The distance is the point where the cursor ray is nearest to the axis line, so the part stays under the cursor in perspective and in ortho.
- **One command per drag.** The release queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy { name, delta }`. The drain (`crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs`) runs it as the `MoveModel::new` of the Model page, with the rotation copied bit for bit. Thus a drag is one undo step, with the same staleness, the same following stock and the same fixture-clash warning as a typed move. There is no new placement path.
- **No history step for:** Escape during a drag (the key is consumed), a drag that ends at its start point, and Move turned off.
- **Turned setups.** When the active setup holds the part turned (#326), the drag occurs in the frame of that setup. The shown delta is rotated back into the document frame, so the part moves along the axis that the user sees.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/1198-drag-to-move.md`: only parts are dragged in this slice, Move mode is off by default, and the preview moves the body only.

## MCP
No new app command, thus no new MCP tool. `MoveModelBy` is a UI queue verb over the existing `MoveModel`. The MCP `move_model` tool (`crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs`) already places a part through `MoveModel`. An agent can make each move that a drag makes.
